chapter: Big band, Chicago players, recordings and gospel
title: African review for public school children
summary: He bought talking drums and turned the album into an African review with conga drummers and dancers, funded by a government grant.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Did you ever try any of those things?

I didn't try -- yeah, I bought a talking drum. I've had about four or five of them things. Right, and then I had a show that we travelled into the public schools with. I put on an African review, and took all the music from the album and transformed it into this review.
I remember when we had a meeting that you attended and I attended at the music department of the public schools.
Yeah, right, right, right, right. And
You talked about bringing jazz into particularly the black schools.

Right, right, right, right. It was a grant from the government that they had at that time. So the African show that we put together, we used six musicians and we did the whole bit. We had the drums and we did the thing and the conga drum, two conga drummers and all of this. And the dances and the songs and everything. It was beautiful, it was really a beautiful thing.
